The phrase "Over one's skis" is an idiomatic expression that means to proceed too far beyond one's capabilities or expertise, often leading to negative consequences. It originates from skiing, where a skier who leans too far forward can lose balance and fall.
General Context: Refers to someone taking on more responsibility or risk than they can handle.
Example: "After making several ambitious promises, she realized she was over her skis."

The observer effect is the disturbance of a system by the act of observing it. To learn anything about a system, an instrument has to interact with it, and the interaction changes what is being measured.
Checking a tire's pressure lets a little air out of the tire.
A mercury thermometer has to absorb or give up heat to reach the temperature of what it measures, so it shifts that temperature slightly.
Seeing an electron takes at least one photon striking it. The collision changes the electron's momentum and position.
Measuring a quantum system changes its state. A system in Superposition is found in a single outcome once it is measured.
In the double-slit experiment, placing a detector at the slits to learn which one each particle passes through erases the interference pattern on the screen.

The observer effect is related to Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, which is a separate result: the uncertainty principle limits how precisely pairs of quantities such as position and momentum can be defined at all, however gently they are measured.

The "observer" is any instrument or interaction that records information. Detectors produce the same effect whether or not a conscious person reads them, and research does not support the claim that consciousness changes physical reality.

A minimal, self-modifying AI coding agent. Stripped of most built-in features (no MCP support, no plan mode); users extend it themselves by writing hook-based extensions the agent loads into its own process.
OpenClaw started as a fork of Pi (originally called Tau) and later adopted Pi directly as its underlying agent core.
Developed under Earendil (Earendil Works), the company founded by Person/Armin Ronacher.

PiAI has no plugin API in the usual sense; it has an extension system, and extensions are the mechanism by which nearly every optional behavior in the agent is expressed. The project describes itself as a "self extensible coding agent", and the extension surface is what that phrase cashes out to.

An extension is a TypeScript module that default-exports (pi: ExtensionAPI) => void | Promise<void>. The host loads it in-process with jiti, the factory registers contributions and subscribes to lifecycle events, and the return values of those event handlers can mutate, veto, or short-circuit what the agent does next.

Source lives in packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/, where three files carry the whole system: types.ts (the public contract), loader.ts (discovery and import), and runner.ts (the host that dispatches events and resolves conflicts).
Extension — the unit of behavior. What most hosts would call a plugin.
Package — the unit of distribution. One package may ship many extensions plus skills, prompt templates, and themes.
ExtensionAPI, conventionally bound to pi — the registration object handed to the factory once, at load time.
ExtensionContext, conventionally bound to ctx — the runtime object handed to every event handler on every invocation.
Contribution — anything registered: a tool, command, shortcut, flag, renderer, or model provider.
Event — both notification and hook. There is no separate hook concept; what distinguishes an interception point from an observation point is only whether the host reads the handler's return value.
